Observations / notes:
BP taken at 10:15 – 148/92. Pulse 74 regular. Client reports she has been taking her usual medication (Amlodipine 5mg) but admits she missed "a few days" last week when she ran out and could not get to the chemist. Advised to restart as prescribed and to see Dr Bell within the next week for a review. Given a written BP diary to complete over the next 7 days. Client asked if she should stop taking the tablets if she feels dizzy – advised NOT to stop without speaking to the GP first. She seemed to understand. Will follow up by phone on Friday 26 May.

Client also mentioned that her daughter is concerned about her memory – "she says I forget things". Client herself feels her memory is fine. Noted for future reference – no further action today unless client raises again.

Signature of staff: P. Okafor

INTAKE RECORD 002

Client name: Marcus Webb
DOB: 03/09/1990 (age 32)
Address: 17 Station Road, Wrenfield, WV1 3LH
Phone: 07700 900456
GP surgery: Wrenfield Health Centre, Dr Osei

Reason for visit: Client came in asking for advice about stopping smoking. States he has been smoking about 15 cigarettes a day for the last 10 years. Has tried to stop twice before – once using nicotine patches (stopped after 3 days because of skin irritation) and once "cold turkey" (lasted 2 weeks). Wants to try again. He has heard about a local stop smoking service but does not know if he needs a referral.

Observations / notes:
Discussed options including local stop smoking clinic at the Wrenfield Library on Tuesdays (drop-in, no referral needed, 10am–12pm). Client seemed keen. Gave him a leaflet with the details. Also discussed using e-cigarettes as a harm reduction approach – client said he had not considered this and would think about it. He was not ready to set a quit date today. Suggested he come back to the next session (17 June) to let us know how he got on. He said he would try to attend. No other health concerns raised.

Client appeared well and in good spirits. No physical examination required.

The site register lists the Brampton Community Centre address as 12 Brampton Road, Wrenfield, WV1 2AB. Record status: current.

Signature of staff: M. Chen

INTAKE RECORD 003

Client name: Evelyn Hartley
DOB: 22/11/1944 (age 78)
Address: Flat 3, 26 Brampton Road, Wrenfield, WV1 2AB
Phone: 07700 900789
GP surgery: Wrenfield Health Centre, Dr Bell

Reason for visit: Client attended for a medication review. She is on a repeat prescription for Levothyroxine 50mcg and Ramipril 5mg. She says she has been feeling "very tired" and has noticed some swelling in her ankles in the evenings. She also mentioned that she has lost her repeat prescription slip and needs a new one.

Observations / notes:
BP taken at 11:00 – 132/78. Pulse 68 regular. Ankles slightly swollen but no pitting oedema noted. Client says the swelling is worse at the end of the day and goes down overnight. Advised to elevate her legs when sitting. She asked if the Ramipril could be causing the swelling – explained that it is not a common side effect but she should mention it to Dr Bell. Gave her a new repeat prescription request form to take to the surgery. Also advised her to have a blood test for her thyroid function before her next review – she has not had one since December 2022. Client said she would book it this week.

Client also mentioned that she is finding it difficult to open the new-style medicine bottles – she has arthritis in her hands. Suggested asking the chemist for easy-open lids. She seemed pleased with this advice. Will mention to her GP if she raises it again.

No other concerns. Client was chatty and seemed in good spirits.

The following KPIs shall be monitored by the joint steering group at each quarterly meeting:

1. **Medicines Reconciliation:** At least 95% of patients discharged from hospital to Greenfield Surgery’s registered list have a completed medicines reconciliation within 7 days of discharge, with Northgate Pharmacy providing the reconciled list to the surgery.

2. **Repeat Prescription Accuracy:** At least 99% of repeat prescriptions processed by Northgate Pharmacy are dispensed without error, as defined by the pharmacy’s standard operating procedures.

---

**6. PERFORMANCE MONITORING AND SERVICE EXPECTATIONS**

6.1 The Project shall be delivered in accordance with the service expectations set out in Schedule 2. The Trust shall use reasonable endeavours to meet the performance indicators listed in that Schedule, and shall report against them in the format prescribed by the Council from time to time.

6.2 Performance indicators shall be reviewed at the annual review meeting provided for in Clause 9, and may be amended by written agreement of the parties. Any such amendment shall be recorded in a variation note signed by both parties and appended to this Agreement.

6.3 The Trust shall provide the Council with access to such records and premises as the Council may reasonably require to verify compliance with the performance indicators and the service expectations.

6.4 Where a performance indicator is not met, the Trust shall provide a written explanation to the Council within 20 working days of becoming aware of the shortfall, together with a proposed action plan to address the matter. The Council shall consider any such explanation in good faith and may agree an alternative target or timetable where appropriate.

6.5 The parties acknowledge that the Project is a community health outreach initiative and that some performance indicators may be affected by factors outside the Trust's reasonable control, including seasonal demand, staff availability and public health guidance. In such circumstances, the Trust shall notify the Council as soon as reasonably practicable and shall provide such supporting information as the Council may reasonably request.

---

**7. REPORTING AND ACCOUNTABILITY**

7.1 The Trust shall submit to the Council:

(a) an interim report, no later than 31 December 2023, covering the period from the Effective Date to 30 November 2023;

(b) a final report, no later than 31 May 2024, covering the remainder of the Funding Period.

7.2 Each report shall include:

(a) a narrative summary of activities undertaken and outcomes achieved against the performance indicators;

(b) a breakdown of expenditure against the budget set out in Schedule 3, including any variances and explanations for such variances;

(c) a statement of any issues or risks affecting delivery of the Project, together with proposed mitigations;

(d) such other information as the Council may reasonably request in writing.

7.3 The interim report shall be submitted in draft form to the Council's project lead at least 10 working days before the due date, to allow for comment and review. The Trust shall incorporate reasonable comments received within 5 working days of the draft being shared.

7.4 The final report shall be accompanied by a statement signed by the Trust's Finance Director confirming that the grant funding has been used only for the purposes set out in Schedule 1 and in accordance with the budget breakdown set out in Schedule 3.

7.5 The Trust shall maintain a project log, recording key activities, attendances and outcomes, and shall make this log available to the Council on request.

---

**8. INSURANCE AND INDEMNITY**

8.1 The Trust shall maintain, at its own expense, appropriate public liability insurance and employer's liability insurance throughout the Funding Period, and shall provide evidence of such insurance to the Council upon request.

8.2 The Trust shall indemnify the Council against any claims, losses or damages arising from the negligent acts or omissions of the Trust, its staff or its volunteers in connection with the Project, except to the extent that such claims, losses or damages arise from the negligence or breach of statutory duty of the Council.

**PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT – GREENFIELD SURGERY**

**Renewal and Amendment Agreement**

**Date:** 1 April 2024

**Parties:**

1. **West Cumbria Health Trust** ("the Trust"), a charitable incorporated organisation registered in England and Wales (registered charity number 1154321), whose principal office is at 14 Lowther Street, Whitehaven, Cumbria, CA28 7AH; and

2. **Greenfield Surgery** ("the Practice"), a GP practice operating from Greenfield Health Centre, 3 Oaklands Road, Egremont, Cumbria, CA22 2UY.

**Background**

(A) The Trust and the Practice entered into a Partnership Agreement dated 1 April 2022 ("the Original Agreement") for the provision of community health outreach services in the Egremont and surrounding area.

(B) The Parties wish to renew the Original Agreement for a further period, with amendments reflecting changes to the services, contact arrangements and reporting requirements.

(C) This Agreement records the renewal and the amendments, and the Original Agreement shall continue in force as varied by this Agreement.

**1. INTERPRETATION**

1.1 Terms defined in the Original Agreement shall have the same meaning in this Agreement unless otherwise defined or amended below.

1.2 In this Agreement:

"**Agreement**" means the Original Agreement as varied by this renewal;

"**Effective Date**" means 1 April 2024;

"**Funding Period**" means the period from the Effective Date to 31 March 2025;

"**Project**" means the community health outreach project as described in Schedule 1 of the Original Agreement, as amended by Schedule 1 of this Agreement;

"**Review Date**" means 31 March 2025.

**2. RENEWAL AND TERM**

2.1 The Original Agreement, as varied by this Agreement, is renewed for the Funding Period commencing on the Effective Date and expiring on the Review Date.

2.2 The Parties shall review the operation of the Agreement on or before the Review Date and may agree to a further renewal in writing.

2.3 Termination provisions in clause 11 of the Original Agreement shall continue to apply, provided that any notice served after the Effective Date shall take effect no later than the Review Date unless the Parties otherwise agree in writing.

**3. AMENDMENTS TO SERVICES**

3.1 Schedule 1 of the Original Agreement is amended by replacing the description of the outreach service with the description set out in Schedule 1 of this Agreement. The principal changes are:

(a) the addition of a weekly wellbeing drop-in session at the Community Hall, Main Street, Egremont, to commence no later than 1 June 2024;

(b) the removal of the term-time school-based healthy eating workshops, which were discontinued by mutual consent in November 2023;

(c) an increase in the target number of home visits for housebound patients from 12 to 15 per month, reflecting demand identified during the first year of the Project.

3.2 For the avoidance of doubt, all other services described in Schedule 1 of the Original Agreement remain unchanged.

**4. AMENDMENTS TO PERFORMANCE INDICATORS**

4.1 Schedule 2 of the Original Agreement is amended as follows:

(a) Indicator 4 (number of patients referred to the Practice's social prescriber) is revised from "at least 8 per quarter" to "at least 10 per quarter";

(b) Indicator 7 (patient satisfaction score) is revised from "at least 85%" to "at least 88%";

(c) a new Indicator 10 is added: "at least 20 attendees per month at the weekly wellbeing drop-in session, averaged over each quarter";

(d) the baseline data for Indicator 4 is updated to reflect actual performance in the year ending 31 March 2024.

**5. AMENDMENTS TO FUNDING AND BUDGET**

5.1 The budget set out in Schedule 3 of the Original Agreement is replaced by the budget set out in Schedule 3 of this Agreement.
